title: one-bus-per-instance-hosts-every-shim
owner: codemother owns the care of this seam (ruling 2026-09-06 codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code); CC/Opus builds. Akien owns the design choice already made: one bus per cairn instance, spanning hosts later.
intention: One bus per cairn instance: a single bus process on the box that every device's shim registers into and every device reaches over IPC, so that the nine private in-process buses collapse onto one pipe.
why: Akien's launch chain, told for the second time 2026-09-06 and recorded verbatim at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md. Cast the same day so the intention carries a ticket (CLAUDE.md: an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect).
traces_to: Law 6 (one owner: the bus owns the ring and the flush, at one address) and Law 1 (one pipe means one place to learn from — Akien 2026-09-06: 'if everything goes thru one pipe, we learn faster'); CLAUDE.md Rules-awaiting-physics: an IOU without a ticket is the defect this cast retires. Ruled-in-substance the same day: 'one bus per cairn instance' (I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md).

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate — cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_one_bus_process.py (new): spawns two couriers, asserts one pid, one ring hit across processes, zero db reads; plus test_ring.py staying green. Feeds back on failure: a red names which of the four falsifier teeth broke. Durability: committed in cairn; seal via the tester with source_fingerprint over the bus package.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when: (1) `pgrep -f cairn.devices.cairn.machines.bus` shows exactly one process per instance after any two device commands are run from separate terminals; (2) a message posted by device A's shim from process P1 is read by device B's shim from process P2 without touching the db (ring hit, measured by the bus's own receipts); (3) grep for `BusDevice(` outside the bus package and its proofs returns zero callers; (4) `cairn librarian show status` round-trips through the socket in under 1s with no private beat (today's private beat costs 89.3s, measured 2026-09-06). WRONG INTENT if a second host cannot join the same instance's bus without a code change to the addressing — the design already intends the six-box swarm.

questions.a: Three named, all standing. (1) One process can host every shim without one device's probes stalling the courier path — load-bearing; the builder keeps the socket service off the beat thread, and the falsifier's sub-1s round trip measures it. (2) A unix socket is enough — true for one box; the socket path carries the instance name so multi-host is an addressing change (I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md, resolved paragraph). (3) The flock guard from guard.claim_singleton transfers unchanged to a second resident — it is home-parameterized, so yes.

Two points were asserted wrapped and are not: what the bus process does with a shim whose device module fails to import (today: bench under the loop's staleness rule) — resolved by keeping that rule where it is, the loop's, since the bus hosts the shim but the loop still beats it; and how a courier authenticates as its device — not wrapped, deliberately: one box, one user, the socket's file mode is the gate until multi-host, and the ticket says so rather than inventing an auth scheme.

Consulted the lab (recompiled 2026-09-06). The ring cast 7dfa6e1c638d assumed 'single-process, not IPC' — its why (zero-db delivery) survives, its where changes; a distinction, recorded on both. launchers charter's superclaude spawn of the loop: not exclusive, the flock reconciles two callers. bus_client._wire's docstring 'one seam to change': this IS that change. No Law collides; Law 6 is served (one owner of the ring at one address).

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) the socket path — `~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/0/bus.sock`, instance segment never optional; (b) the wire format — one JSON object per line, request {device, verbs:[...], hot:bool} → reply {ok, text, json}; (c) which existing line to copy for the spawn — launchers/superclaude's systemd-run block, unit name cairn-bus; (d) the order of work — first make BusDevice servable over the socket with the ring intact (test_ring.py must stay green), then make connect_bus a client, then delete the in-process construction, measuring the nine callers to zero; (e) what NOT to do — no change to the ground loop package, no new poller, no per-device socket. All five now written into the ticket's how.

constraints: No change to the ground loop's contents: pulse, control flags, devices-found list — ever (Akien 2026-09-06).
One pipe: device → IPC → own shim → bus → addressee's shim → IPC → addressee; the db alone is exempt (volume).
how: The bus becomes a resident process the way the ground loop already is: claimed once per instance by an flock (reuse guard.claim_singleton on the bus's own instance home), listening on a unix socket under ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/0/. Shims live inside that process; a device launcher (devices/<device>/bin/<device>) ensures the bus process is up, registers the device's shim in it if absent, then couriers the verb line in over the socket and prints the reply. bus_client.connect_bus() stops constructing BusDevice + GroundLoopDevice and becomes a client of the socket (its docstring already calls _wire 'one seam to change'). The ring stays in the bus process; flush on pulse stays the bus shim's act. The instance name rides the socket path so a later multi-host instance is an address change, not a redesign.
links: 7dfa6e1c638d bus ring cast (its 'not IPC' assumption retires here; its zero-db why survives)
watchme: none, because the operational signal (bus process count over time) is a deterministic pgrep the proof exercises, and the seal's source_fingerprint (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/validations/) expires it when bus.py or the proof changes; when the socket exists, the ground_loop's existing liveness probe shape (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/probes/) is the template for a bus liveness probe, cast then, not now

intent.what: One bus per cairn instance: a single bus process on the box that every device's shim registers into and every device reaches over IPC, so that the nine private in-process buses collapse onto one pipe.

challenge.better_approach: Looked at two: (i) keep in-process buses and let them all flush to the one db — that is the shape Akien ruled out in the same breath ('one pipe'), and it keeps nine rings that never meet; (ii) make the db the bus (LISTEN/NOTIFY only) — already the store's job and the reason the db gets its pass; it gives up the 'instantly, no db access' ring. A resident bus process with the ring in it is the smallest thing that satisfies both his sentences.
challenge.prior_art: In-house: the ground loop is already a resident singleton claimed by flock (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/guard.py) and spawned as a transient user unit by launchers/superclaude (charter launchers--intention+why.json, ruling 2026-08-11: transient, never system-level) — the bus process reuses both mechanisms verbatim. The ring buffer is built and proven (bus.py _ring, test_ring.py, cast 7dfa6e1c638d awaiting review). codemother's mail-dir shim is the one existing device→shim IPC (primitive, no reply). Ticket 0d16e513ff26 the-heartbeat-outlives-its-caller is the parenting precedent. Field: this is a plain unix-socket daemon; nothing to graft.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That one process can host every shim without one device's shim blocking the others — today a shim's on_pulse runs probes inline (89s beats measured). If a slow probe stalls the bus process, one pipe becomes one bottleneck; the builder must keep the courier path off the beat thread. Also assumes the socket, not TCP, is enough for now — true on one box, and the multi-host horizon is explicitly not built here.
challenge.real_collision: The ring cast 7dfa6e1c638d states 'the bus is single-process, in-memory delivery via hooks, not IPC' as an assumption. Its why was zero-db delivery; this ticket keeps that why (the ring lives in the one process) and changes only where the callers sit. A distinction to record, not exclusive-and-terminal; the launch-chain intention already lists that assumption under 'what this retires'. The launchers charter's superclaude spawn of the ground loop is not a collision either: two launchers may both spawn, the flock makes it one loop.

why_beneath_the_why: Akien 2026-09-06: 'if everything goes thru one pipe, we learn faster' and 'everythign automatically lazy inits' — the operator types one command and the system stands itself up behind it, on one pipe, with nothing to remember.

decisions.text: Reconciled with Akien's 2026-09-30 ruling (bus charter filed edges a+b; ground_loop charter falsifier 6). (1) The ground loop no longer beats shims or benches a device on staleness — both were deleted (bae622881f03, efb670ff1dd8); a shim whose component fails to import answers its caller with the import error, loudly, and nothing retries it on a clock. (2) The ring flush is reached by the ground loop's SPAWNED pulse: the bus process answers a verb `flush` on its socket, and the pulse entry `python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.bus pulse` sends it and exits (no bus process running = nothing in any ring = exit 0, recorded). The pulse never delivers; delivery stays the event in-process (falsifier 5). The spawn itself is the ground loop's ticket, cast after this one.
decisions.step: unlisted: ruling 2026-09-30 moves the flush onto the spawned pulse

decisions.text: SERVER at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py. HOME is env CAIRN_BUS_HOME else ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/0 (instance segment never optional); the socket is <home>/bus.sock (mode 0600 — one box, one user, the file mode is the gate) and the claim is <home>/bus.lock taken with fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) — the same shape as ground_loop/guard.py claim_singleton, written again in server.py and cited, never imported (RULE 1: guard is the ground loop's internal). A refused claim exits 3 (the unit's SuccessExitStatus, the loop's convention). A stale bus.sock from a dead process is unlinked only AFTER the claim is won. Wire: one JSON object per line each way over socketserver.ThreadingUnixStreamServer; every request carries 'op' and 'root' (the caller's class root). Ops: call {method, kwargs} -> {ok, json} for post|read|request|undelivered|record_delivery|digest|list|toggle; hold {devices:[names]} or {shim:'module:Class'} -> {ok, held:[device ids]} (a held shim is pulsed once in the bus process, which wires its delivery); verbs {device or shim, verbs:[...]} -> {ok, exit, text, json} = the held shim's resolve(verbs); flush -> {ok, json: bus.flush()}; stats -> {ok, json:{pid, root, table, posted, delivered, db_reads, ring_depth, receipts:[envelope ids in the ring's receipts]}}; shutdown -> flush, reply, exit 0. Any exception is {ok:false, error:'Type: text'} (Law 7: loud, never empty). A name with no shim is {ok:false, error:'no shim answers to <name>'} which the client raises as LookupError. ENTRY cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/__main__.py: 'serve [--home H] [--scratch]' (scratch = the bus over BusDevice.scratch('bus_proc'), a throwaway table for proofs) and 'pulse [--home H]' (D1).
decisions.step: unlisted: the bus process — address, claim, wire

decisions.text: BUS.PY, three changes, test_ring.py stays green. (1) PENDING: a dict _pending{id: envelope} of personal envelopes not yet receipted — post() adds, record_delivery() removes, flush() does NOT clear it; a set _loaded of addressees whose db backlog has been read. undelivered(to=X) reads the db anti-join ONCE for X (or once for everyone when to is None), merges those rows into _pending, marks X loaded, and from then on answers from _pending alone, oldest first, limit applied. So a poke delivers with zero db reads and a failed delivery is still retried on the next poke. (2) COUNTER: self._db_reads += 1 at every store.read call in read() and undelivered(); exposed as the property db_reads. (3) ATOMIC FLUSH: one threading.Lock around ring/receipt mutation; flush swaps self._ring and self._ring_receipts for fresh lists under the lock and writes the swapped lists outside it, so a post during a flush lands in the next one instead of being cleared unseen.
decisions.step: unlisted: the bus keeps undelivered mail in memory after one db read

decisions.text: STALE: at start the server records its class root (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]) and its code stamp = the newest st_mtime over every *.py under <root>/cairn and <root>/bin, skipping __pycache__ (measured 2026-10-02: 373 files, 3ms). Every request whose root differs from the server's, or arriving after the stamp has moved past the start stamp, is answered {ok:false, stale:true, root:<server root>} and nothing else. The CLIENT, on stale, sends shutdown and re-ensures the bus from ITS OWN class root, then retries the request once. So a hollow worktree, or a commit that changed a shim, gets a bus running the code that asked — one bus at a time, the flock still decides — and no resident process answers with code nobody is running.
decisions.step: unlisted: the bus serves the code that asks

decisions.text: CLIENT at cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py (a tool: speaks only the socket, imports nothing from the bus package). exchange(request, home=None) -> dict: connect to <home>/bus.sock, send one line with root=this file's class root (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]), read one line; ConnectionRefusedError/FileNotFoundError propagate. ensure_bus(home=None, *, scratch=False): if exchange({op:stats}) answers, return; else spawn 'python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.bus serve --home <home> [--scratch]' with ensure_ground_loop's systemd-run block copied (unit = env CAIRN_BUS_UNIT else cairn-bus, -p SuccessExitStatus=3, --working-directory <class root>, StandardOutput/Error append:~/.cairn/logs/bus.log, reset-failed retry when the name is held, setsid Popen fall-through), then wait up to 15s for the socket to answer stats (a bounded wait in the launcher, not a poller). RemoteBus(home=None): methods post, read, request, undelivered, record_delivery, digest, list, toggle each = call op with those kwargs; flush(), stats(), shutdown(), hold(*devices), hold_shim('module:Class'), verbs(device_or_shim, argv). wire_delivery(device_id, _hook) = hold(device_id): delivery happens in the bus process, and the local hook is dropped by design. unwire_delivery is a no-op. ring_depth reads stats. Every op goes through one _call that does the stale retry.

CLI_MAIN in cairn/tools/base/shim.py: cli_main(shim_cls, argv) constructs NO shim. It calls the client tool: ensure_bus(); reply = RemoteBus().verbs(f'{shim_cls.__module__}:{shim_cls.__name__}', argv); prints reply['text'] to stdout on exit 0 else stderr; returns reply['exit']. A transport failure (no bus after ensure) prints the error to stderr and returns 1. The import of cairn.tools.bus_client.remote is deferred inside cli_main so importing shim.py stays light.
decisions.step: unlisted: the launcher line is couriered

decisions.text: CALLERS. bus_client.py: _wire returns (RemoteBus after ensure_bus(), DeviceRoster(remote)); connect_bus(devices, beat) holds the named devices in the bus process (hold), returns the RemoteBus; reach(*devices) = hold(*devices) and LookupError from a no-shim refusal; connect_system returns (remote, roster) without holding a BusShim — the bus shim lives in the bus process; inference_bus and models_stack unchanged above reach. roster.py: unchanged except it no longer expects the bus's own shim held; pulse() on a shim with a RemoteBus wires via hold. transitions.py:1714: the crossing notification posts through cairn.tools.bus_client.connect_bus() (no devices, beat False). inbox.py:516 read_email: connect_bus(beat=False).undelivered(limit=10000). bin/cmd/probescan scan_mail: its import path cairn.devices.bus.bus is already dead (no such module) — it reads traffic through connect_bus(beat=False).read() and receipts are dropped from the triage. The four proofs that build a BusDevice outside the bus package use BusDevice.scratch(...) (the classmethod; not a BusDevice( call) where they need a private table — db_domain test_scratch_cannot_outlive_its_process.py:103, librarian test_librarian_chat.py:411, tester test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py:177, system_rackmount test_system_rackmount.py:76 — each stays green.
decisions.step: unlisted: the callers go to zero

decisions.text: CONCURRENCY: ThreadingUnixStreamServer gives each connection its own thread; the bus's one Lock guards only ring/receipt/pending mutation (microseconds), never a handler. Each held shim gets its own threading.RLock taken around its poke and its verbs, so a slow librarian answer blocks only librarian traffic; RLock because a handler that posts to itself re-enters on the same thread.
decisions.step: unlisted: one device's slowness does not stall the courier

decisions.text: open-b49db843959b is ANSWERED (Akien, 2026-09-24): "the bus is its own process; the ground loop is heartbeat plus device list, nothing more". So the bus process is a second resident unit, cairn-bus, separate from the ground loop — which is what decisions 1, 2 and 5 build: the loop never hosts a shim, and its spawned pulse only asks the bus process to flush (decision 1).

cli_main resolves a shim class whose __module__ is '__main__' in the calling process: such a class has no address the bus process can import. Every launcher's shim lives in a module, so only a proof's inline fixture (test_root_verbs, test_root_verb_vocabulary) takes this branch; decision 6 holds for every other class.
decisions.step: unlisted: a shim defined in __main__ has no address

decisions.text: remote.py names the systemd unit per bus home: CAIRN_BUS_UNIT if set, 'cairn-bus' when the home is the live instance's (~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/0 under the account's home from the password database, never HOME), else 'cairn-bus-<sha1(home)[:10]>'. A bus at any home but the live one is spawned with --scratch. Measured 2026-10-03: a proof under a scratch HOME took the name cairn-bus and the next scratch HOME got 'spawned: none'; and a scratch-HOME bus over the live table would drain live mail into a throwaway instance.
decisions.step: unlisted: one unit and one table per bus home

decisions.text: Amends decision 2's 'pulsed once'. The bus process holds a shim two ways: for a verb line (op verbs, cli_main) it is held COLD — constructed, never wired — and for mail (op hold: connect_bus, reach, RemoteBus.wire_delivery) its delivery is wired once by shim._wire_delivery(), never by on_pulse. Measured 2026-10-03 with test_root_verb_vocabulary: pulsing on hold fired probes and announced menus, which woke cairn and cc and stamped last_known on a cold list, and cc's list then failed ('NoneType' has no attribute 'introspect'). A pulse is the ground loop's, and the loop beats no shim.
decisions.step: unlisted: holding to answer is cold, holding for mail wires

decisions.text: Decision 7 named BusDevice.scratch for all four proofs; two measure something else. tester test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py:177 is a LIVE check (nothing stands undelivered to the tester on the live bus), so it asks through connect_bus(beat=False).undelivered(to='tester'); a scratch bus would make it vacuous. system_rackmount builds a fresh BusDevice.scratch per rig (it built a fresh BusDevice per rig before), and the one shared table goes. test_root_verb_vocabulary's fixture shuts its scratch HOME's bus down with the HOME. probescan's scan_mail derives 'picked up' as personal envelopes absent from bus.undelivered(), since the receipt table is the bus's internal (RULE 1).
decisions.step: unlisted: two proofs re-pointed by what they measure

decisions.text: D14: the crossing door no longer posts a crossing notice to harbor_master. Measured 2026-10-02: transitions posted through a private BusDevice whose ring nothing flushed — 563 notices reached the bus table up to 2026-09-02, none since — while the harbor's scan from disk kept its register current. Posting through the one bus process instead puts remote.py's socket on the inspector's verdict path (inspector imports transitions; test_inspector_nexus reds), and leaving the private BusDevice reds this ticket's own clause that nothing outside the bus package calls BusDevice. The journal append is the crossing's record; the harbor's 'crossing' verb now has no sender, and a harbor that learns crossings from the journal event is the commit fan-out's work (8a372dee4c79), not this ticket's. The operator inbox reads undelivered through reach(); probescan and the tester proof ask through reach() too.
D3 adds no method beyond the three named changes: BusDevice.scratch(prefix, device_id) already stands at HEAD (bus.py:202) and the re-pointed proofs use it as it is.

D7 as amended by D14: the crossing door posts nothing to harbor_master — that post is removed from transitions.py; the crossing's record is the journal, and a harbor that learns crossings from it is ticket 8a372dee4c79's (the commit fan-out), not this ticket's. The other D7 callers move to the bus process through bus_client as written.

The proof is not built at this step: it stands already, committed red at 56542f8e (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_one_bus_process.py, with its fixture shim bus_proof_echo.py) — four clauses plus D1 and the stale-root tooth, run as a plain script like its neighbours. The build turns it green; nothing in it changes.
decisions.step: unlisted: create cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_one_bus_process.py with four falsifier teeth

decisions.text: D5's block is the one at cairn/tools/base/shim.py ensure_ground_loop (line 82), spelled again in cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py _spawn, never imported (RULE 1): systemd-run --user --quiet --unit <unit> --working-directory <class root> --setenv=HOME --setenv=PATH -p SuccessExitStatus=3 -p StandardOutput/StandardError=append:<log> -- python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.bus serve --home <home>; on 'already loaded'/'fragment file' it runs systemctl --user reset-failed <unit>.service and retries once, and if the name is still held it waits — bounded by the start wait — for the unit to go inactive, then spawns again; with no systemd-run it falls through to Popen(start_new_session=True) with stdout/stderr appended to the log.
